problem:
The volume of water in a tank was recorded over time for $25$ minutes, starting from time $t=0$ minutes. The following table shows the volume $V(t)$, in liters, recorded at time $t.$

| $t$ | $0$ | $5$ | $10$ | $15$ | $20$ | $25$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $V(t)$ | $120$ | $150$ | $165$ | $180$ | $215$ | $240$ |

Approximate the rate of change of volume at time $t=5$ using a forward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

At $t=5,$ the estimated rate of change is {{field-1}} liters per minute.
worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
{V}^{′}(t)≈\frac{V(t+h)-V(t)}{h}
$$

at the point $t=5.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}^{′}(5) & ≈\frac{V(5+5)-V(5)}{5} \\  & =\frac{V(10)-V(5)}{5} \\  & =\frac{165-150}{5} \\  & =\frac{15}{5} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, at $t=5$ the rate of change was approximately $3$ liters per minute.
